angle: Movement translation: each player's Combine 40 speed profile (first-second distance, 2.5-s drive distance, top speed) vs the same phase on his own random NFL snaps (alignment- and route-matched), across WR/TE/DL/DB/OL; WR top end picked as the clearest group with a production outcome; then whether translation (Speed Realization) explains yards per route beyond pick, weight and the official 40, with and without ball-in-hand running. DL rush drive distance vs pressure as the cross-position check.
metric_name: Speed Realization (SR) = NFL route top end (mean of a WR's 3 fastest random routes, snap to throw, route x alignment adjusted) / his year-standardized Combine 40 top speed
headline_number: WR 40 top speed -> NFL route top end rho = 0.28 [0.00, 0.51], n = 63, within-class perm p = 0.012, 0.30/0.29/0.22 by class, replicates 0.32 on high-|EPA| half; SR vs shrunk YPRR beyond pick/weight/40 = 0.40 [0.13, 0.60] (only test of 27 surviving Holm, p = 0.030) when top speed includes the whole play, but 0.22 [-0.05, 0.46] snap-to-throw, 0.15 untargeted, 0.07 high-|EPA| half (MDE 0.35); out-of-class dR2 +0.046 (whole play) vs -0.001 (snap to throw). Blind 2025 card: 75% of WRs inside the 80% band projected from the 40.
what_changed_from_previous: New metric and position focus, building on the round-1 winner's translation framing and applying its judge top_changes. (1) Uses the ETL's stored sample_kind flag and the new 40-snap sample (20 random snaps/player vs 6), so game-side reliabilities are 0.46-0.59 instead of 0.07. (2) Burst defined as first-second distance; three phases x five groups translation map with noise ceilings and 80%-power MDE bands, and the group pick rule is stated explicitly. (3) The DL 'translation' (raw 0.52) is shown to be size and alignment (0.04 after both). (4) Every null is reported with MDE and TOST and framed as 'cannot detect'. (5) A tracked-vs-official 40 test (adds 0.03 partial, 0.005 out-of-class R2). (6) LOCO slopes per class, a within-class permutation p, and replication on the high-|EPA| half. (7) Baseline hygiene: weight year-standardized, with/without slot share, per-fold R2 incl. 2025, outcome season-to-season reliability, EB-shrunk YPRR by routes. (8) A new 'ball trap' finding: the realization-production link exists only when top speed includes catch-and-run (31% of top-3 whole-play snaps were targets vs 17% of routes); the same pattern holds for DL rush speed vs pressure (0.23 -> 0.11 without pressure snaps). (9) A blind 2025 draft-room band card with flags and an explicit 'what would change our mind' rule. (10) 5 figures + 1 table: hero cards with z-bars, snap counts and takeaway titles; fit line plus bootstrap band; n in titles; text >= 9 pt; captions shortened.
open_risks: Translation is modest (0.28; 0.22 after weight, CI includes 0) and out-of-class R2 for levels is ~0.02; the 40 ranks receivers but the official 40 already carries the signal.
Headline is again partly a null: the only surviving test is the contaminated whole-play version; the clean versions sit below the MDE of 0.35, and only the high-|EPA| replication is TOST-equivalent.

Forking paths: the window and aggregation (snap-to-throw, top-3) were chosen after exploration that included production results; all four windows are reported, but the sensitivity is real (arrival-window translation is 0.14 on random routes vs 0.44 on the high-|EPA| half).

Snap-to-throw lasts a median 2.6 s, so the 'top end' partly measures acceleration on quick-game routes; no ball or opponent tracking, so coverage and leverage are only handled through route x alignment cells.
The full baseline over-fits at n = 63 (pick alone has higher out-of-class R2 than the full baseline); the 2025 class has one season; QB quality and injuries are not modeled.
DB shows similar top-end translation (0.31) but has no coverage outcome; TE n = 20 is too small for any verdict.
